claim: R2-26 (a) put a raised way's ring-end foot on ground part 0's `margin` chain (§2.7 `RaisedFoot`, l. 2296–2299: 'its ground end a `raised_foot` vertex placed by `splitThrough` on ground part 0's `margin` chain at the deck's end point … no ramp or stair is drawn there'). It hands the frame growth to 'the raised way's re-derivation re-placing both ends of that foot on the new rings'. The kernel's frame growth runs first and leaves the vertex undefined. Batch (b) on part 0 (§3.2 (9), l. 3563–3566) strips the old ring's `margin` rows, and 'a stretch left with no row is deleted'. At a ring-end foot, part 0 carries no ramp and no way, so the foot's vertex loses both its edges and keeps only its `raised_foot` row. §3.2 (9)'s vertex rule (l. 3573) says such a vertex 'stays'. But the arena's vertex record has `out: one outgoing half-edge` (§2.2, l. 592), and no text defines a vertex with no edge. §2.2 rule 3's dissolution covers only degree-2 vertices, and §3.4's strip of a far end 'restores the edge it split', which is gone. The raised part's own end is an antenna end of its spine, as a through-road's is; part 0's end is not. Between the growth and §4.11's re-derivation, part 0 therefore holds a vertex the kernel cannot represent, and the walks, the index, §3.10's rows and its later removal are undefined there. This is canon's named combination C-raised-frame (edges.json, UNDEFINED), opened by this round's foot on the ring (principle (11)).
required_change: §3.2 (9): after 'A vertex of an old chain that keeps a row or another edge stays — a through-road's end on the old ring is an antenna end until §4.11 continues its way — and every other dissolves or stays by §2.2 rule 3.' add: 'A raised way's ground foot at a deck end on the old ring (§2.7 `RaisedFoot`) — a `raised_foot` vertex the strip would leave with its row and no edge — is never left so. On part 0, batch (b)'s insertion (the new ring with S1's water) and its strip are then two L0 batches, and between them one batch at the foot row's level moves each such foot: its row is stripped by `removeEdges` on its `VertexRef`, the vertex dissolving back into the old ring (§2.2 rule 3), and added by `splitThrough` on the new ring at that ring's point nearest it (ties by lattice address). The deck end on the raised part's own old ring stays an antenna end of its spine, as a through-road's end does. The raised way's re-derivation (§4.11) then extends the deck to the new ring and re-places both ends of that foot (§2.7), so both ends resolve at every stage end (§3.10's stored-references row).' In (b) itself, replace '`Plat.frame` takes the new frame as this batch commits' with '`Plat.frame` takes the new frame as its last batch commits'. (Another shape is acceptable, e.g. a defined isolated vertex with `out` = −1 that the re-derivation deletes, provided both ends resolve at every stage end; VKr2-02 tests it.)

claim: §3.1's code list (l. 3450) gives `'E_NO_PATH' // with the closest reached point [F-ROUTE]`. The bracket names the classes the code reaches, as the brackets of `E_KEPT`, `E_LEVEL` and `E_SELF_INTERSECT` name the dry run. Pipeline's round-2 text (VPC-R1-23) in II.7.6 step 3 (l. 21252–21256) now routes the same code elsewhere: 'a route the search does not find (`E_NO_PATH`, §3.1 …): the dry run refuses with its reason … (F-EDIT, §5.2)'. At generation, the connection stage runs the same connector for an undercity lifeline (§7.3 item 9 (d)'s *At generation*, l. 10932–10934). A neighbourhood whose lifeline finds no route is F-VOID's 'a neighbourhood left without a lifeline' (§5.2, l. 8978). The code's home thus names one consumer of three.
required_change: §3.1, l. 3450: replace '// with the closest reached point [F-ROUTE]' with '// with the closest reached point [F-ROUTE; F-VOID — an undercity lifeline's dug connector at generation, II.7.5, II.7.6; in an edit the dry run's refusal, F-EDIT — II.7.6 step 3]'.
